target.title: fix(qa-channel): honor canonical thread action fields
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes QA channel thread and edit actions that did not consume the canonical fields emitted by the shared message runner. A requested `threadName` silently became `QA thread`, while thread replies and edits using `message` failed before reaching the QA bus.

## Why This Change Was Made

The adapter now prefers the shared `target`, `threadName`, and `message` contract. Thread creation and replies resolve destinations through the existing QA target parser, including its conversation ownership and conflicting-thread checks.

`qaChannelMessageActions` is a published public adapter surface, so this does not remove its shipped aliases. Direct callers using `channelId`/`threadId`/`to`, `title`, or `text` continue to work; canonical `threadName` and `message` win when both forms are supplied. The `title` schema field remains as an explicitly deprecated alias.

## User Impact

QA scenarios can create named threads, reply through the returned thread target, and edit messages through the normal CLI/message-tool path. Existing direct adapter consumers keep their prior behavior.

## Evidence

- Immutable secretless proof: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29668482200
  - before `20677baf7666c97a2b80af599522145d83c08845`: canonical create fell back to `QA thread`; canonical reply/edit failed
  - after `0ec795d1c6e9beeb1fb56e63edfefc4502cd0988`: canonical create/reply/edit succeed through `runMessageAction` -> QA channel -> QA bus
  - the same run records legacy-only create/reply/edit succeeding before and after, plus canonical-over-legacy precedence on the new head
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.plugin-dispatch.test.ts` (50 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-channel/src/channel.test.ts -t 'exposes thread and message actions|keeps the shipped thread and edit aliases'` (2 passed, 19 skipped)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` (11 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/contracts/boundary-invariants.test.ts` (14 passed)
- `node scripts/check-tsgo-core-boundary.mjs`, targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.

Repository-wide caller search found production QA actions entering through shared dispatch; direct `handleAction` calls are owner tests. Because the adapter is nevertheless exported from `extensions/qa-channel/api.ts` and shipped in `v2026.7.1`, the final patch deliberately retains and tests those public aliases.

An independent Codex adversarial review first rejected the canonical-only version for compatibility. After adding canonical-first alias handling, deprecated schema metadata, owner-local precedence/legacy tests, and the boundary-correct generic runner test, the reviewer returned GO with no actionable findings. A follow-up review also cleared the schema-union type fix before the final push.

AI-assisted: Codex was used for implementation, contract tracing, tests, and adversarial review. I reviewed the resulting behavior and understand the change.
